why: A multiset can form a palindrome when at most one letter has an odd count. Each change fixes two odd letters, so the minimum is (#odd letters)//2. Greedy choice: sort the odd letters and turn the larger half into the smaller half (the middle one, if any, becomes the centre), then lay out the smallest palindrome from the counts.
hints: Only letters with odd counts are a problem. Changing one letter can fix two of them at once.

With odd letters sorted o1 < o2 < ... < ok, change o_k to o_1, o_{k-1} to o_2, and so on. If k is odd, the median o_{(k+1)/2} stays odd and becomes the centre. That uses the minimum number of changes and makes the letters as small as possible.
Then build half = letters a..z, each repeated count//2 times, and return half + centre + reverse(half). O(n + 26).
pitfalls: Change the largest odd letters into the smallest ones. Doing it the other way round gives a valid but larger palindrome.
When the length is odd, exactly one odd letter stays as the centre. Pick the median odd letter, not the smallest.
Do not add extra changes. The count of changes must stay minimal even if more changes would give a smaller string.
